title: Analyzer version: the cache key must track resolver output without a manual bump (DEC-303 a79 follow-up)
description: Record-only ordinary follow-up under DEC-303 (a79) (opum-ai/opum-doc#2082, ODOC-640), NOT a hold item. The systemic gap measured for GCLI-140: src/python/indexer.ts:30 has held PYTHON_ANALYZER_VERSION = "3" since GCLI-89 (#139, 4f313f7), the only commit that ever set it; GCLI-116 through GCLI-146 changed resolution output without bumping it, and both cache keys (cacheKey.analyzerVersion) include it, so a warm cache keeps serving edges an older resolver produced. proposal (choose at build): derive the cache key from a content hash of the resolver sources (src/python/calls.ts, indexer.ts, modules.ts, symbols.ts, parse.ts) instead of, or beside, the manual constant, so any resolver change invalidates caches with no judgement call; the constant can stay as a human-readable marker. FALLBACK if the source hash is too coarse (a comment change would invalidate): a check that fails when the fixture-suite resolver output changes and the version does not — the committed digest approach. The GCLI-140 PR bumps the constant to "4" (a79 Q-D A) but does not fix the mechanism.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The cache key changes whenever any resolver source changes (a content hash of the resolver sources, or an equivalent mechanism), so a warm cache can never serve edges an older resolver produced
A test proves the mechanism: a one-byte resolver source change moves the key (or the digest check fails) while a non-resolver change does not
Resolution output is unchanged: the five-pin delta is identical to the parent head
